title: IPAM keeps the address of removed containers (about 7% of short-lived containers), exhausting a bridge network's subnet
body:
### Issue Description

On a rootful bridge network, podman keeps the IPAM allocation of a fraction of containers after they are removed. The containers go through a normal lifecycle with no error logged (`create`, `died`, `cleanup`, `remove` events), but their address stays in `ipam.db`. Over about two days this filled a `/24`, and every new container on the network then failed with:

```
Error attaching to container <id>: preparing container <id> for attach: IPAM error: failed to find free IP in range: 10.95.0.1 - 10.95.0.254
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

I don't have a minimal reproducer yet. The workload: GitLab Runner 19.5.2 with the docker executor, talking to the rootful podman API socket (`/run/podman/podman.sock`), with `network_mode` set to a dedicated bridge network created by a Quadlet `.network` unit (`Subnet=10.95.0.0/24`). Each CI job creates several short-lived containers (the runner's helper containers and the build container), all removed when the job ends. About 3,300 helper containers were created on the network over two days.

### Describe the results you received

After about two days, a copy of `/run/containers/networks/ipam.db` held 253 allocations in the network's subnet bucket, one per container id, and the network's `ids` bucket listed the same 253 containers. None of them existed: `podman ps -a --filter network=<network>` was empty. For all 253 ids the journal has a `container create` event, and 252 of them also have `died`, `cleanup` and `remove`, with no warning or error from podman at any point. 250 were the runner's helper containers and 3 build containers: about 7.6% of the helper containers created since boot (250 of 3,291), at a steady rate of roughly 110 a day.

Separately, after `podman network rm` of the now empty network, re-creating it failed with `subnet 10.95.0.0/24 is already used on the host`: the network's bridge interface was still present and holding the gateway address, and had to be removed with `ip link delete` before the network could be created again.

### Describe the results you expected

A removed container's address is released, so a subnet sized for the concurrent containers never fills; and `podman network rm` removes the network's bridge interface.

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

Fedora CoreOS (Fedora 44 based), rootful, netavark backend with the nftables firewall driver, cgroup v2, SELinux enforcing. Not tested on 6.1.4: this host runs the 5.8.9 that Fedora CoreOS ships.

### Additional information

- The leak was invisible while the runners used the default `podman` network (a `/16`), and because `ipam.db` lives in `/run`, every reboot cleared it. A smaller dedicated network made it fail within days.
- During the hours it filled, the API service also answered the runner with "no such container" (271 times in 43 minutes) and "can only create exec sessions on running containers" (133 times), which may point to container removal racing the cleanup path. The leaked containers' own journal entries show no error, though.
- Possibly related, both fixed long ago: #18615 (addresses consumed by a restarting container, fixed by #20384) and #15708. containers/common#2341 (deallocate IPs on a setup error) is in this version; this case has no setup error.
- I can share a copy of `ipam.db` (container ids and private addresses only) and journal excerpts if that helps.

comments.body: Dup of https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/30106 most likely? Fell free to test the linked PR there

Thanks, that looks like the same bug. Same setup here: GitLab Runner's docker executor against the rootful podman socket, but with `network_mode` set to one persistent bridge network instead of `FF_NETWORK_PER_BUILD`. So instead of leftover bridges, the leak showed up as IPAM allocations piling up on that one network.

I checked the journal for the 253 containers that still held an address: each of them has exactly one `network disconnect` event (253 of 253), next to its `died` and `cleanup` events. So the skipped teardown in #30106 also leaves the container's address allocated in `ipam.db`, not only the bridge, and the `podman network rm` leftover bridge I mentioned fits the same path.

Closing this one as a duplicate of #30106 is fine with me.
